Answer: B
Reason: In a 74-year-old patient, a solitary thin-walled cavitary lesion in the lung is highly suspicious for bronchogenic carcinoma (specifically squamous cell carcinoma) with central necrosis, whereas tuberculosis typically presents with thick-walled cavities and upper lobe predominance, and lung abscesses usually have thick walls with air-fluid levels.
